title: The Siyum: wild and domestic, and finishing Baitza
label: Siyum
summary: The final shiur and siyum on Masechta Baitza. Buying and measuring on Yom Tov without doing business, why it can be better to let people err unknowingly, Shabsai bar Marinus and the rich of Bavel, and the three whose lives are not lives. The masechta ends with the wild and domestic animals, read as two kinds of learners: those who leave home to learn and those who work by day and learn every night.
key_ideas: On Yom Tov one may buy without naming a price or a measure, so it is not business.
Where a rebuke won't help, it can be better to let people err unknowingly.
The Gemara lists three whose lives are not lives.
Wild and domestic animals are read as two kinds of learners: those who leave home to learn, and those who work by day and learn every night.
